first.rationale: Activation and onboarding completion are both down 4-6% QoQ, indicating a product-side friction issue that pricing alone won't solve. However, competitive pricing pressure on SMB segments is acute and immediate. memory_73 showed promotional pricing worked for price-sensitive SMB but had methodological caveats that warrant re-verification before scaling. memory_86 showed onboarding shortening improved both completion and adoption—this addresses root friction. Running a small_guarded_test on promotional_pricing lets us defend against churn in the price-sensitive cohort while we simultaneously investigate whether the activation decline stems from onboarding friction (memory_31, memory_86, memory_91 all support this vector). Promotional pricing is fastest to deploy and protects revenue this week, but the downstream risk is that it trains customers to expect discounts and doesn't fix underlying product friction. A small test preserves our ability to pivot if the data shows the activation issue is structural rather than price-driven. Verification of memory_73 and memory_86 is critical: one to confirm promotional pricing efficacy given the methodological note, one to establish the baseline lift from onboarding improvements so we can measure interaction effects.
